title: Photonic circuits become trainable AI hardware
key_facts: A physics-based in situ learning method directly measures optical gradients with photonic integrated circuits.
It allows diverse circuit topologies to be trained after fabrication.
The hardware achieved matrix design, multiwavelength computation and rapid meta-learning.
It does so without requiring a full digital model of the circuit.
The summary relates to Zhou, T. et al., Nat. Comput. Sci. (2026), 'Photonic neuromorphic learning via generalized in situ physical gradient descent'.
Only the summary was readable; the page is behind a subscription.
quote_evidence: A physics-based in situ learning method is demonstrated that directly measures optical gradients with photonic integrated circuits, allowing diverse circuit topologies to be trained after fabrication.
This hardware achieves matrix design, multiwavelength computation and rapid meta-learning without requiring a full digital model of the circuit.
why_it_matters_hint: A light-based chip can be trained after it is built without simulating it digitally first.
